tools.name: activate_skill
tools.description: Activate a Skill by injecting its exact instructions into the conversation as a tagged tool result. Activated Skill procedure is subordinate to Vesicle host rules, the active Engine/Harness contract, and the user's explicit request; it cannot add tools or change permissions. Use read_skill_resource for files bundled with an activated Skill. Bundled scripts run only via run_skill_script under the user's current permission mode. Activate a Skill only when its catalog description matches the user's task.

name.description: Skill name from the available Skill catalog.

tools.exercise: Freeze a catalog containing fixture-skill, activate it, and verify exact tagged content and activation identity; an unknown name cannot activate.
conditions: The active Engine/runtime surface must expose this definition; permissions never grant a missing capability.

header.description: Very short label for the question, such as "Engine", "Scope", or "Style".

question.description: The complete question to ask the user. Keep it clear, specific, and phrased as a question.

options.description: Mutually exclusive choices. Do not include Skip or open-ended fallback options; the host appends those fallbacks automatically.

label.description: Short user-visible option label, ideally 1 to 5 words.

description.description: One sentence explaining the option's impact or tradeoff.

tools.exercise: Persist the pending question, restart, and answer once; options and exact tool-call pairing survive.

tools.name: grep_files
tools.description: Search allowed UTF-8 project files for literal text or a JavaScript regular expression. Returns matching lines with optional context, or switch outputMode to list matching files or count hits per file.

path.description: Project-relative path beginning with one of: assets, source_materials, workspace, novels, reports, test_runs, tmp, or a skills/<name>/... path into the read-only mount of Skills activated in this session. Do not use '.' or absolute paths; other paths are rejected. Project-root VESICLE*.md files are host-managed Persistent Instructions, not file-tool paths.

pattern.description: Search pattern. Interpreted literally unless regex is true.

regex.description: Treat pattern as a JavaScript regular expression. Defaults to false.

caseSensitive.description: Whether matching is case-sensitive. Defaults to false.

recursive.description: Whether to search directories recursively. Defaults to true.

maxMatches.description: Maximum matches to return. Defaults to 50 and is capped at 200. In files_with_matches and count modes, limits the number of files instead.

contextLines.description: Lines of context to show before and after each match. Defaults to 0 (no context). Capped at 10. Only affects outputMode 'content'.

outputMode.description: Output shape. 'content' returns match entries with text (default). 'files_with_matches' returns only file paths that contain matches. 'count' returns per-file match counts.

tools.exercise: Search a multibyte fixture tree with bounded context/results; each declared outputMode and regex/case option retains its documented meaning.
conditions: The active Engine/runtime surface must expose this definition; permissions never grant a missing capability.

tools.name: list_directory

path.description: Use '.' for the virtual root, or a directory beginning with one of: assets, source_materials, workspace, novels, reports, test_runs, tmp, or a skills/<name>/ path into the read-only mount of Skills activated in this session. Example: workspace or assets/templates.

recursive.description: Whether to list descendants recursively. Defaults to false.

detail.description: Output detail. 'full' returns typed entries and metadata (default); 'names' returns file paths only. For path '.', names returns the logical root names for discovery. Both modes return fileCount, directoryCount, otherCount, empty, and truncation metadata.

tools.exercise: List the requested directory at the selected detail/depth without exposing host-private or escaped paths.

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file from an allowed Vesicle project directory. Use startLine/endLine to read a line range, or offsetBytes/maxBytes to read a bounded byte slice without loading the whole file (preferred for very large files or giant single-line payloads).

path.description: Project-relative path beginning with one of: assets, source_materials, workspace, novels, reports, test_runs, tmp, or a skills/<name>/... path into the read-only mount of Skills activated in this session. Do not use '.' or absolute paths; other paths are rejected. Project-root VESICLE*.md files are host-managed Persistent Instructions, not file-tool paths.

startLine.description: Optional 1-based first line to read (ignored when maxBytes is given).

endLine.description: Optional 1-based last line to read, inclusive (ignored when maxBytes is given).

offsetBytes.description: Optional non-negative byte offset for a bounded slice read (requires maxBytes; project files only).

maxBytes.description: Optional maximum bytes to read from offsetBytes. When set, reads a bounded byte slice (project files only) instead of a line range and never loads the whole file.

tools.name: request_confirmation
tools.description: Pause the workflow and ask the user to confirm or reject the current blueprint, plan, or phase artifact before proceeding. Rejection may include change requests or discussion; empty rejection is valid and means the model should ask what to change. Only call this when the active engine prompt instructs a stop gate (e.g. ETL blueprint-confirmation or phase-confirmation). Do not call it for ordinary conversation.

gate.description: The stop gate identifier declared by the active engine profile (e.g. "blueprint-confirmation"). Must match a gate the engine declared.

summary.description: Compact human-readable summary of what is being confirmed. Rendered verbatim above the gate options. For ETL: include the current blueprint or phase artifact, written file paths when applicable, and the proposed next phase.

options.description: Optional custom option labels. When omitted the host shows the standard Confirm/Reject pair. Each option carries a canonical decision the host knows how to act on.

tools.exercise: Pause only if this gate is declared by the Engine; acceptance/rejection yields one durable result before another provider request.
conditions: The active Engine/runtime surface must expose this definition; permissions never grant a missing capability.

tools.name: request_engine_switch
tools.description: Pause the workflow and ask the user to confirm switching to another Prism engine profile. Use this when a different engine should own the next workflow step. The host will not switch silently: confirmed switches take effect on future turns, while rejection is returned to the current engine so it can discuss or revise the handoff.

targetEngine.description: The Prism engine profile that should handle future turns.

reason.description: Why this engine switch is appropriate now.

handoffSummary.description: Compact handoff state for the target engine: relevant artifacts, decisions, current workflow state, and what continuity must be preserved.

recommendedNextAction.description: Optional concrete next action the target engine should take after the user confirms.

tools.exercise: Request a host handoff without immediately changing Engine; Stage is excluded from this tool enum and requires its separate bootstrap.
conditions: The active Engine/runtime surface must expose this definition; permissions never grant a missing capability.

The script runs as structured argv through the resolved interpreter (no shell) from the project root, with the current host user's process authority, environment filtering, timeout, and output caps. Every call is subject to the active Vesicle permission mode. Inspect the script source with read_skill_resource before running it.

args.description: Optional arguments passed to the script verbatim (never through a shell).

timeoutMs.description: Wall-clock timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 120000.

tools.exercise: Execute an activated script through resolved argv and permission/process boundaries; path scope is not a host-process sandbox.

tools.name: update_instructions
tools.description: Write or delete one Persistent Instruction target (scope=user|project, engine=all|<engine>). Replaces or removes the whole target file; an empty content string is an explicit empty override. Optional ifMatchSha256 ('absent' or a 64-hex hash) guards concurrent edits; omit it for an intentional overwrite. A successful mutation records one previous state under instruction-backups, but /rewind does not restore Persistent Instructions; recovery from that backup is manual. The summary is a one-line human reason. Use this only for explicit, user-requested persistent workflow management — not to change host capabilities or modify ordinary play.

content.description: Required for write; forbidden for delete.

tools.exercise: Approve a bounded named-target update, then exercise explicit ifMatchSha256 conflicts and deletion; preserve backups and truthful results.

allowedPaths.description: Optional path regexes to include, such as /docs/.*.
